newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA STUMBLE AS GILLESPIE TAKES FIVE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA STUMBLE AS GILLESPIE TAKES FIVE.

text.p: Australian fast bowler Jason Gillespie claimed his first five-wicket haul in only his fourth test as South Africa were bundled out for 209 on the first day of the second test in Port Elizabeth on Friday.
The performance totally vindicated captain Mark Taylor's decision to put the hosts in to bat on a damp, well-grassed pitch and by the close the Australians had reached 10 for one in reply.

Opener Matthew Hayden was dismissed for a duck as Daryll Cullinan pulled off a smart slip catch off Shaun Pollock. But it was still an excellent day for the Australians who already lead the three-test series 1-0 after a comprehensive victory in the first test in Johannesburg.

Gillespie shared four wickets with fellow pace man Glenn McGrath in the morning session but then grabbed the first three wickets after lunch to finish the day with five for 54 from 23 hostile and accurate overs.
Out-of-form opener Gary Kirsten was the first to go when he could only fend a Gillespie lifter into the hands of Hayden at short-leg for a duck in the sixth over of the innings.
Jacques Kallis also failed to trouble the scorers. Another Gillespie lifter saw him lob a simple catch to Greg Blewett at backward short-leg.
Opener Adam Bacher survived an impassioned appeal for a catch at the wicket before he had scored but then fell to McGrath for 11, caught in the gully by Matthew Elliott.

With wickets falling at 13, 17 and 21, a grim-faced South African captain Hansie Cronje strode to the wicket but his determination amounted to nothing -- literally. He became the third duck when he was bowled off an inside edge by McGrath to leave his team on 22 for four.
Cullinan and Herschelle Gibbs launched a mini-revival either side of lunch before Gillespie found a thick edge and Shane Warne took the catch in the gully to remove Cullinan for 34.
Gillespie then removed Gibbs's off stump with a classic off-cutter for 31 and had Shaun Pollock lbw next delivery -- the fourth duck of the innings.
At that point South Africa were 95 for seven but the veterans Brian McMillan and Dave Richardson offered desperate resistance with an eighth-wicket partnership of 85.
But it was too little too late as leg-spinner Warne took the last three wickets in quick succession to finish with three for 62 from 23.4 overs.

First the 37-year-old Richardson, three runs short of his half-century, skied an off-drive to a tumbling McGrath and then the 33-year-old McMillan, who missed the first test because of injury, pulled Warne to Steve Waugh at deep square-leg.
His 55 came from 108 deliveries and the innings closed shortly after when Allan Donald prodded a simple return catch to the bowler.
